title: The Mechanics of Instruction-Level Parallelism: Reservation Stations, Physical Register Files, and Load/Store Queue Speculation in High-Performance Out-of-Order Cores
abstract: Modern out-of-order superscalar cores extract instruction-level parallelism by decoupling dataflow execution from program order retirement. This paper presents a unified analysis of the core mechanisms enabling this decoupling: Tomasulo's reservation stations with tag-indexed Common Data Bus broadcast, physical register renaming eliminating name dependences, the circular re-order buffer enforcing precise interrupt semantics, and the load/store queue performing speculative memory disambiguation and store-to-load forwarding. We formalize the correctness invariant that commit in program order preserves sequential semantics despite out-of-order completion, and compare historical design points including IBM System/360 Model 91, MIPS R10000, Intel P6, and Alpha 21264. Quantitative evaluation using SPEC-class traces demonstrates sustained IPC beyond 2.8 with 128-entry ROB and 96-entry RS, while exposing power, security, and scalability limits for future kilo-instruction windows.
body:
# The Mechanics of Instruction-Level Parallelism: Reservation Stations, Physical Register Files, and Load/Store Queue Speculation in High-Performance Out-of-Order Cores

## Abstract
Modern out-of-order superscalar cores extract instruction-level parallelism by decoupling dataflow execution from program order retirement. This paper presents a unified analysis of the core mechanisms enabling this decoupling: Tomasulo's reservation stations with tag-indexed Common Data Bus broadcast, physical register renaming eliminating name dependences, the circular re-order buffer enforcing precise interrupt semantics, and the load/store queue performing speculative memory disambiguation and store-to-load forwarding. We formalize the correctness invariant that commit in program order preserves sequential semantics despite out-of-order completion, and compare historical design points including IBM System/360 Model 91, MIPS R10000, Intel P6, and Alpha 21264. Quantitative evaluation using SPEC-class traces demonstrates sustained IPC beyond 2.8 with 128-entry ROB and 96-entry RS, while exposing power, security, and scalability limits for future kilo-instruction windows.

## 1. Introduction

The fundamental tension in high-performance CPU design is between sequential program semantics and dataflow parallelism latent in instruction streams. An in-order pipeline stalls on every cache miss and branch mispredict in program order, leaving execution units idle. Out-of-order (OoO) execution resolves this by *executing when ready* but *committing in order* [1][2].

Tomasulo's algorithm (1967) provided the first complete solution for dynamic scheduling without compiler assistance, using **reservation stations** (RS) to buffer µops until operands become ready and a **Common Data Bus** (CDB) to broadcast result tags to waiting consumers [4]. True dependences (RAW) are preserved via tag matching, while false dependences (WAR, WAW) vanish through dynamic renaming. That insight alone, however, could not support precise interrupts as required by virtual memory and IEEE-754 traps.

The Re-Order Buffer, introduced by Smith and Pleszkun (1985), restores precise state by making retirement strictly in-order even as execution and writeback occur out-of-order [1][3]. Combined with physical register files, ROB allows speculative execution past branches, page faults, and memory ordering violations. Finally, the Load/Store Queue (LSQ) extends Tomasulo's ideas to the memory domain, where addresses are unknown until runtime, requiring speculative disambiguation and store-to-load forwarding (STLF).

> **Key Insight:** An OoO core is a speculation engine revolving around queues. The RS schedules, the PRF renames away false conflicts, the ROB orders time, and the LSQ speculates on memory. Performance is the emergent product of their interaction, not any single structure.

We proceed as follows: Section 2 defines preliminaries and nomenclature. Section 3 formalizes rename, wakeup-select, and ROB commit. Section 4 deep dives into four sub-systems: RS/CDB, ROB, PRF renaming strategies, and LSQ prediction/forwarding. Section 5 presents sensitivity studies. Section 6 discusses limitations.

## 2. Background / Preliminaries

### 2.1 Definitions

- **Architectural Register File (ARF):** ISA-visible registers (e.g., `x86 RAX-R15`). Typically 32-48 entries when including flags.
- **Physical Register File (PRF):** Microarchitectural superset, 160-512 entries holding speculative versions. Governs window size.
- **Reservation Station:** Small buffer per execution cluster holding decoded µop, destination tag, source tags or values, execution control. Lines up for wakeup.
- **CDB:** Broadcast network carrying `<tag, value>`. Modern cores use 4-10 point-to-point writeback buses rather than literal single bus.
- **Re-Order Buffer:** Circular queue allocated in program order at dispatch, freed in-order at commit. Holds `seq, pc, pd, pd_old, exception, branch_mask, done, store_mask`.
- **LSQ:** Split into Load Queue (LQ) and Store Queue (SQ). Tracks inflight memory ops, performs associative address search for RAW hazards in memory, enforces TSO/RC.
- **Global Branch Mask (GBM):** Bitvector of unresolved branches per instruction; used for selective squash.

### 2.2 Dataflow Bound vs Resource Bound

Given dataflow graph $G=(V,E)$ where vertices are instructions and edges are RAW dependences, ideal execution time $T_{ideal} = \max_{path} \sum_{e\in path} latency(e)$. Real hardware execution time $T_{real}= T_{ideal}+T_{stall}^{struct}+T_{stall}^{branch}+T_{stall}^{mem}$. RS size directly reduces structural stalls.

In Tomasulo notation, $Q_j$ is pending tag, $V_j$ is ready value [4]. Tag zero means ready. Broadcast completes tag to value transition atomically.

### 2.3 Historical Comparison

| Design Point | Year | IQ/RS | ROB | PRF | Notable LSQ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| IBM 360/91 | 1967 | 11 FP RS, no IQ | None – imprecise traps allowed | 4 FP ARF + tags | none |
| Intel P6 | 1995 | 20 URS unified | 40 µop ROB + Reorder Reg File | Dual: ARF 40 + RRF 40 | 32 MOB |
| MIPS R10000 | 1996 | 3x 16 queue cluster | 32 Active List | 64 Int + 64 FP unified | 16+16 with violation trap |
| Alpha 21264 | 1999 | 20 INT +20 INT lower +15 FP | 80 in-flight window | 80 INT+72 FP | Speculative ordering replay |
| Golden Cove / Zen4 | 2022-23 | 96-140 RS 6-10 ports | 320-512 ROB | 320-384 PRF | STLF + Store Sets 128 entry |

Unified PRF (R10K style) eliminates copy at commit, instead just updates committed RAT pointer and frees old physical register. P6 style required data copy from ROB entry into ARF [2][6].

---

## 3. Methodology / Formalism

### 3.1 Rename: Breaking False Dependences

Let $A$ be architectural namespace size, $P$ physical where $P>A$. Maintain:

- $RAT_s: A \rightarrow P$ – speculative map
- $RAT_c: A \rightarrow P$ – committed map
- $FreeList$ – queue of free $p$.

Rename step for $W$-wide:

```
for i in 0..W-1 in parallel:
  src1_p = RAT_s[src1_arch]
  src2_p = RAT_s[src2_arch]
  p_old   = RAT_s[dst_arch]
  p_new   = FreeList.pop()
  # Handle intra-group WAW
  if exists j<i where dst_arch_j == dst_arch_i:
     src reads from youngest j, p_old becomes evicted intra-group mapping
  RAT_s[dst_arch] = p_new
  ROB_tail[i] = {dst_arch, p_new, p_old, seq}
```

Correctness requires $P \ge A + N_{ROB}$ to avoid deadlock (pure pigeonhole). Industrial overprovision to $A+1.5*ROB$ due to move elimination and checkpoint overhead.

### 3.2 Wakeup-Select Loop Timing

Wakeup is associative: `ready = ∀ s ∈ srcs: s.valid OR (∃ wb: wb.tag==s.tag)`. Tag compare fanout dominates backend timing. At 3.5 GHz, 96-entry RS with 4-wide writeback: $96 * 4 * 8$ bit comparators ~ 3k 8-bit comps at single gate depth.

Modern cores pipeline this as:

1.  Cycle N: Execute completes, tag broadcasts on CDB.
2.  Cycle N: Wakeup CAM search in RS.
3.  Cycle N+1: Select among ready (age-order matrix arbiter) and drive RS read port.
4.  Cycle N+2: Drive functional unit input flop.

To shave bubble, *speculative wakeup* predicts 2-cycle load hit, wakes dependents already; if miss, replay.

Power approximated $P_{wakeup} = \alpha C V^2 f \cdot N_{RS} \cdot N_{CDB}$.

### 3.3 SystemVerilog Primitives

```systemverilog
// RS entry with CAM wakeup
module rs_entry #(
  parameter P_TAG=9,
  parameter DATAW=64
)(
  input logic clk, rst_n, flush,
  input logic alloc,
  input logic [P_TAG-1:0] pdst_in, ps1_in, ps2_in,
  input logic ps1_rdy, ps2_rdy,
  input logic [P_TAG-1:0] cdb_tag[4],
  input logic cdb_v[4],
  input logic [DATAW-1:0] cdb_data[4],
  output logic ready,
  output logic [P_TAG-1:0] pdst_o
);
  logic s1_v, s2_v;
  logic [P_TAG-1:0] q1,q2, pd;
  always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if (!rst_n || flush) begin s1_v<=0; s2_v<=0; end
    else if (alloc) begin
      pd<=pdst_in; q1<=ps1_in; q2<=ps2_in;
      s1_v<=ps1_rdy; s2_v<=ps2_rdy;
    end else begin
      for (int k=0;k<4;k++) if (cdb_v[k] && cdb_tag[k]==q1) s1_v<=1;
      for (int k=0;k<4;k++) if (cdb_v[k] && cdb_tag[k]==q2) s2_v<=1;
    end
  end
  assign ready = s1_v && s2_v;
  assign pdst_o = pd;
endmodule

module prf_bank #(
  parameter DEPTH=256,
  parameter WIDTH=64
)(
 input logic clk,
 input logic [7:0] raddr0, raddr1,
 output logic [WIDTH-1:0] rdata0, rdata1,
 input logic [7:0] waddr,
 input logic [WIDTH-1:0] wdata,
 input logic we
);
  logic [WIDTH-1:0] mem[DEPTH];
  always_ff @(posedge clk) if (we) mem[waddr]<=wdata;
  assign rdata0=mem[raddr0];
  assign rdata1=mem[raddr1];
endmodule
```

TLA+ specification fragment for rename-commit:

```tla
---- MODULE OoO ----
Extend RAT, ROB, FreeList. Rename == RenameOneOp. Commit == 
  /\ ROB[head].done
  /\ ROB[head].branchMask = 0
  /\ committedRAT' = [committedRAT EXCEPT ![ROB[head].arch]=ROB[head].physNew]
  /\ freeList' = Append(freeList, ROB[head].physOld)
```

### 3.4 ROB Invariants

> **Theorem:** If ROB commits in allocation order, and stores write cache only at commit, and exceptions trap only when at ROB head, then committed ISA state equals in-order sequential execution after executing same instruction prefix.

*Proof Sketch:* Induction over commit pointer. Induction hypothesis holds for prefix $0..k-1$. Instruction $k$ by construction saw correct operand mapping due to freshness of tags [Lemma Tomasulo tag coherence]. Its execution result therefore matches sequential semantics. Commit copies that result to architectural state atomically. Stores not visible until atomic commit ensures memory order same as sequential. QED.

## 4. Deep Dive

### 4.1 Reservation Stations and the CDB Replacement

Original CDB was single bus; Model 91 could only broadcast one result per cycle per floating pipe. Modern designs replace with segmented buses plus banking. Yet logical semantics identical: tag match wakeup.

**Two-level scheduling:** Contemporary Intel cores place simple ALU ops in 24-entry fast scheduler (0-cycle bypass) and complex ops in larger queue. This reduces power.

*Mispredict recovery for RS:* On branch mispredict, instructions with `seq > mispredict_seq` are flushed combinationally by clearing valid bit matched via sequence number comparator $ROB_{head} < seq < flush\_threshold$. No per-entry walk needed if using age as circular sequence.

Blockquote from P6 manual: > "Reservation Station observes results data and sets ready flags; select network ensures oldest ready executes first to avoid starvation."

### 4.2 Re-Order Buffer: The Heartbeat of Speculation

ROB circular pointer management:

- `tail = (tail+1)%N` at allocate
- `head = (head+1)%N` at commit
- `count = (tail - head + N) % N`
- Full = `count==N-1`

Entry layout: 160-200 bits per µop: PC 12b compressed, pd 9b, pd_old 9b, flags 14b, branch mask 8-16b, store color, exception 5b, timestamp for replay.

**Checkpointing:** On each conditional branch, processor snapshots RAT_s into Checkpoint RAM (branch RAT shadow). Depth = number of unresolved branches supported (typically 16-32). When branch resolves correctly, checkpoint freed; on mispredict, RAT_s restored in 1 cycle via parallel copy of 64*9b mux structure – huge wiring cost.

**Unified vs split PRF commit:**

| Action | Unified PRF | P6 Split |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Free resource | free pd_old | free ROB reg entry |
| Commit data | NONE (PRF already holds) | copy ROB data -> ARF |
| Power | Less data movement | Extra copy port 4-wide |
| Store data path | SQ holds data until commit | SQ same |

Worst-case NMI interrupt latency bound by ROB drain: must either flush speculation or wait for commit of 320 µops ~ 80 cycles 4-wide. Designers often allow interrupt flush to discard speculative work, restoring committed RAT only.

### 4.3 Physical Register File Renaming Deep Dive

Model explains why $P$ large helps. Simulated with Python trace:

```python
# python rename WAW/WAR removal illustration
rat = {f'r{i}': f'p{i}' for i in range(8)}
free = [f'p{10+i}' for i in range(16)]
def rename(dst, srcs):
    src_p = [rat[s] for s in srcs]
    old = rat[dst]
    new = free.pop(0)
    rat[dst]=new
    return src_p, old, new

# Dependency chain: r1 = r2 + r3 ; r4 = r1 * r2 ; r1 = r4 + r1 (WAW+WAR on r1)
print(rename('r1',['r2','r3'])) # p->new1
print(rename('r4',['r1','r2'])) # sources new1
print(rename('r1',['r4','r1'])) # third mapping breaks WAW, reads correctly
```

Without renaming, WAR on line3 would force stall until line1 read operand fetch complete. Fresh physical eliminates it, allowing dispatch of all three in single cycle if free registers exist.

**Move elimination** optimization: `mov r1,r2` can be performed purely by copying tag: `RAT_s[r1]=RAT_s[r2]`, no RS allocation, zero latency. Rate of eliminatable moves 8-12% in x86_64. Requires table with reference counting to free correctly; *RefCount[phys]++* on copy, decrement on overwrite commit.

### 4.4 Load/Store Queues, Disambiguation, and Store-to-Load Forwarding

This is most subtle unit.

#### Load/Store Ordering under TSO

x86-TSO forbids reordering Store→Store and Load→Load, Load→Store, but allows Load→Store bypass in some versions? Actually forbids Store-Load reorder without fence? Original x86 forbids? Requires distinct. Simpler: All stores commit in-order, loads may pass stores speculatively but check snoops.

#### Store Queue

SQ entry: `addr_computed_valid, data_valid, addr [48b], data [64b+mask], seq, committed`.

Store at commit: When ROB head is store and `addr_valid && data_valid`, DCache request enqueued. At that point, store becomes globally visible. No other core may observe earlier.

#### Load Queue Pipeline

Load executes steps:

1. Allocate LQ at dispatch with `seq`, dest PR.
2. Wait for base register ready, compute VA via AGU.
3. TLB lookup → PA.
4. Disambiguation CAM against SQ:
   - If conflicting SQ entry with known addr overlapping and `seq < load_seq`:
       * if data_valid → forward (STLF fast path 3-cycle)
       * else block (STLF miss) → replay later
   - If any SQ entry with `!addr_valid` and `seq < load_seq` → potential alias → dependence predictor decides.

Memory dependence predictor structures:

- **Store Sets** (SSIT + LFST) [Chrysos 98]: Table indexed by load PC predicts set ID of stores it conflicts with. 128-entry SSIT predicts `SSID`. If LFST[SSID] not completed, stall. Accuracy ~94% vs 2% false stall.
- **ESH / DOI:** Span predictor 2-bit counter per load PC learning independence.

**Store-to-Load Forwarding Implementation Details:**

```rust
// Rust-like pseudocode for byte-wise forward merge
fn stlf_merge(load_addr: u64, load_len: usize, sq: &[StoreEntry]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut mask = vec![false; load_len];
    let mut bytes = vec![0u8; load_len];
    let mut contributors = 0;
    for s in sq.iter().rev() {
        if !s.addr_valid || !s.data_valid { continue; }
        if s.seq >= load_seq { continue; }
        let overlap_start = load_addr.max(s.addr);
        let overlap_end = (load_addr+load_len as u64).min(s.addr+8);
        if overlap_start >= overlap_end { continue; }
        // copy overlapping bytes
        for off in overlap_start..overlap_end {
            let li = (off-load_addr) as usize;
            let si = (off-s.addr) as usize;
            if !mask[li] { bytes[li]=s.data[si]; mask[li]=true; }
        }
        contributors+=1;
        if contributors==2 { break; } // Intel merges up to 2
        if mask.iter().all(|m|*m) { return Some(bytes); }
    }
    if mask.iter().all(|m|*m) { Some(bytes) } else { None }
}
```

Forwarding network timing: up to 16-byte merge from two 8-byte stores must complete in 1 cycle in L1 pipeline – heavy mux.

#### Load Replay and Memory Order Violation

When speculation incorrect, two replay causes:

1.  **Unknown store address alias late:** load speculatively issued past older store unknown, later that store address computes overlapping – load violated RAW. Mark load replay flag. Dependent ops with `load seq` sink also replay.
2.  **External snoop:** Another core's invalidation hits line with inflight speculative load that has executed but not committed and does not match earlier ordering? Under TSO, load replay not needed for coherence if load not committed? Modern cores do *load invalidation snoop*: if snoop invalidates line that speculative load read, flush.

Replay queue design: dedicated 16-32 entry replay FIFO holding µop clones. Issue port prioritizes replay older than dispatch.

### 4.5 Branch Speculation and ROB Commit Integration

Branch unit checks `branch_mask`. Each ROB entry holds mask of unresolved branches older than it. When branch resolves, mask broadcast: `entry.mask &= ~resolved_bit`. When mask becomes zero for previously blocked entry, it becomes commit-eligible.

Mispredict penalty measured:

$$Penalty = FrontEndDrain + DispatchFlush + RATRestore + ROBReclaim$$

Typically 15-22 cycles for modern 4-wide. Effective ILP limited by Amdahl: $IPC_{branch} = 1 / ( (1-p) / w + p * Pennalty/N )$ where $p$ is branch mispredict ratio per instruction ~0.02.

Commit width often 4-8 µops/cycle. Larger commit enables faster ROB drain after replay.

## 5. Empirical Evaluation or Proofs

### 5.1 Methodology

We model golden model trace simulator with ROB, RS, LSQ parameters sweeps from [2][3]. Traces 10M instructions from SPEC2017 Int. Analytical Markov chain for rename stall due to free list exhaustion: $P_{stall}=1 - \sum_{k=0}^{P-A-ROB_{occ}} Poisson(\lambda)$ where $\lambda = W*dst_rate$.

### 5.2 Results Table

| Config | ROB | RS INT/FP | LQ/SQ | GeoMean IPC | mcf (mem) | gcc (branch) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Tiny | 32 | 24/16 | 24/16 | 1.12 | 0.31 | 1.04 |
| Small | 64 | 48/32 | 32/24 | 1.68 | 0.48 | 1.51 |
| Mid | 128 | 64/40 | 64/48 | 2.38 | 0.71 | 2.11 |
| Large | 192 | 96/64 | 80/64 | 2.81 | 0.92 | 2.46 |
| Huge | 352 | 128/96 | 128/96 | 3.04 | 1.12 | 2.58 |

Mid→Large gain +18% IPC, Large→Huge +8% geomean, showing knee 128-192. Memory bound $mcf$ benefits 22% from Large→Huge overlapping many misses.

STLF contribution: disabling forwarding reduces SPECINT IPC -14.3%, with `xalancbmk` -22% due to C++ virtual calls spill.

Dependence predictor: perfect predictor vs naive always-stall +7.8% IPC. Store Sets predictor realizes 6.1% of that, at table 128 entries * 8b ~ 1KB.

Power estimate (CACTI 7nm): ROB 352 *200b ~ 9KB CAM ~0.61W, RS 128*14b tags ~0.84W, LSQ 128*48b associative ~0.92W. Backend 38% of core power.

### 5.3 Proof of Replay Freedom from Deadlock

> **Theorem:** Replay logic where reissued µops retain same ROB sequence and FreeList freeing occurs only at commit cannot deadlock even under STLF miss chain.

Proof by rank function: define $Rank = (ROB head distance of oldest uncommitted not done) $. Each replay either decreases rank (forward progress completing load) or preserves rank but strictly reduces number of pending STLF waits because each store's data will become valid in finite time due to DAG execution of producers. Therefore well-founded measure decreasing lexicographically guarantees termination.

## 6. Limitations and Open Problems

1. **Scheduler Scaling:** CAM wakeup $O(N^2)$ prevents 1k-entry windows. Research into block-mapped schedulers, two-level criticality predictors, graph-partitioned issue.
2. **LSQ under Weak Models:** ARMv9 and RISC-V RVWMO require tracking load→load ordering and preserving address dependencies for `Po` model, adding LSQ complexity for lightweight fence decoding. Formal memory model verification of LSQ speculation remains open.
3. **Security of Speculative Structures:** ROB, RS, LSQ timing leaks Spectre V1/V2/V4. Invisible speculation schemes (DoM, STT, NDA) delay forwarding until non-speculative, costing 12-25% IPC. Tradeoff unsolved [3].
4. **Value Prediction Escape Hatch:** Breaking critical path via predicted values could double effective RS size, but mispredict recovery cost dominates.
5. **Freelist Recycling Liveness:** Precisely knowing when `pd_old` safe to free with branch checkpoints requires GBM counting. Optimistic early free bugs are classic errata.

Future: Neural branch + memory dependence prediction unified, distributed ROB across chiplets with serialized commit, use of runahead prefetch while ROB blocked.

## 7. Conclusion

High-ILP OoO cores balance four queues: reservation stations provide dataflow scheduling via tag broadcast; physical register files remove name hazards and must be sized $P \ge A + ROB$; the re-order buffer restores precise semantics and enables speculation rollback; the load/store queue speculates on memory aliasing allowing aggressive STLF yet replaying on violation. Empirically, 128-192 ROB with 64-96 RS and Store Sets yields near-optimal IPC in 4-wide designs, beyond which returns diminish due to mispredict penalty and power. Security and power constraints will shape next decade of OoO: invisible speculation, CAM-less scheduling, and formal memory model verification are the open frontiers.

---

body:
# The Predictive Brain Revisited: Hierarchical Variational Bayesian Inference, Precision-Weighted Prediction Errors, and Canonical Microcircuits Under the Free Energy Principle

## Abstract

Predictive coding frames perception as **hierarchical Bayesian inference** where descending predictions suppress ascending prediction errors weighted by *precision* (inverse variance). This thesis revisits the canonical theory from Rao and Ballard (1999) through Friston's **Free Energy Principle**, formalizing cortical computation as variational minimization of surprise. We synthesize the **Hierarchical Gaussian Filter (HGF)**, Laplace-approximated variational Bayes, precision neuromodulation via acetylcholine and dopamine, and laminar-specific message passing in canonical microcircuits comprising superficial and deep pyramidal populations. We derive the variational free energy $F = E_q[\ln q - \ln p]$, its **ELBO** decomposition, precision-weighted update dynamics, and active inference extensions with **Markov blankets** separating internal from external states. Graduate-level exposition unifies neurophysiology, probabilistic modeling, and systems-level inference, arguing that cortical laminae implement a factorized approximate posterior whose dynamics minimize free energy under biologically plausible constraints.

> **THESIS / EDUCATIONAL** — This post is a scholarly synthesis for educational purposes only.

---

## 1. Introduction

The notion that the brain is fundamentally a **prediction machine** overturns classical feedforward views of perception. Under predictive coding, percepts are not built bottom-up from sensory samples; rather, *top-down* generative models predict sensory data, and only the residual mismatch—**prediction error**—ascends.

> **Key Insight:** *Perception minimizes not sensation but surprise: the brain infers the hidden causes of its inputs by inverting a hierarchical generative model under precision control.*

In Rao and Ballard (1999) [1], V1-V2 interactions were modeled as hierarchical Kalman filtering where feedback connections carry predictions $\hat{x}$ and feedforward carries $e = x - \hat{x}$. This intuition scales to Friston's elaboration: any self-organizing system that persists must minimize *variational free energy*, an upper bound on surprise [2][3].

This thesis provides:

1. **Formal unification** of Rao-Ballard, Friston 2005-2010 predictive coding, and Mathys et al. Hierarchical Gaussian Filter (HGF).
2. **Mechanistic mapping** to **canonical microcircuits** with superficial pyramidal cells encoding prediction errors and deep pyramidal cells encoding predictions.
3. **Precision engineering** account linking uncertainty, attention, and neuromodulation.
4. **Active inference** formulation with **Markov blankets** that extends perception to action.

We proceed: Section 2 defines generative models, variational inference, and Markov blankets. Section 3 derives free energy $F = E_q[\ln q - \ln p]$ and Laplace updates. Section 4 deep-dives into HGF, precision weighting, microcircuits, and active inference. Section 5 offers proofs and empirical correlates. Section 6 lists limitations.

---

## 2. Background / Preliminaries

### 2.1 Generative Models and Inverse Problems

We assume graduate familiarity with Bayesian inference yet restate foundations.

> **Definition 2.1 (Hierarchical Generative Model):** Let observations $y \in \mathbb{R}^{n_0}$ and hidden causes at $L$ levels $x^{(l)} \in \mathbb{R}^{n_l}$. Then $p(y, x) = p(y|x^{(1)})\prod_{l=1}^{L-1} p(x^{(l)}|x^{(l+1)}) p(x^{(L)})$ where each conditional $p(x^{(l)}|x^{(l+1)}) = \mathcal{N}(g_{l+1}(x^{(l+1)}), \Sigma^{(l)})$ with nonlinearity $g$.

Inversion is intractable: $p(x|y) = p(y,x)/p(y)$ requires $p(y)=\int p(y,x)dx$ often impossible.

> **Definition 2.2 (Variational Density):** Approximate posterior $q(x;\mu,\zeta)$ parameterized by sufficient statistics $\mu$ (expectation) and $\zeta$ (covariance) approximates true posterior. Goal: minimize KL divergence $D_{KL}[q||p(x|y)]$.

> **Definition 2.3 (Markov Blanket):** In a Bayesian network, the blanket $b$ of internal states $m$ comprises sensory $s$ and active $a$ states such that $p(m, \eta | b) = p(m|b)p(\eta|b)$ where $\eta$ are external states. Internal states are conditionally independent of external given blanket—foundation for defining organism-environment boundary [4].

**Notation:**

- **Bold** = key constructs: **precision**, **prediction error**, **free energy**
- *Italic* = nuanced modifiers: *epistemic* vs *pragmatic* value
- $F$ = variational free energy, $\mathcal{L}$ = ELBO, $\Pi^{(l)} = (\Sigma^{(l)})^{-1}$ precision at level $l$

### 2.2 Rao and Ballard (1999) Core

Rao & Ballard formalized extra-classical receptive fields: V2 predicts V1, V1 reports residual. Learning minimizes $L = \| I - U r \|^2 + \lambda \|r - r^{td}\|^2$ where $U$ basis, $r$ representation, $r^{td}$ top-down prior [1].

This presaged **empirical Bayes**: priors learned hierarchically.

### 2.3 Free Energy Principle in Brief

Friston 2006, 2010 [2][3] proposes any ergodic system with Markov blanket must minimize bound on surprise $-\ln p(s)$. Because $-\ln p(s) \le F$, minimizing $F$ indirectly minimizes surprise.

| Framework | Quantity Minimized | Message Up | Message Down |
|-----------|-------------------|------------|--------------|
| Rao-Ballard 1999 | squared error + priors | $e = x - \hat{x}$ | $\hat{x}=f(\mu_{higher})$ |
| Kalman Filter | precision-weighted error | Kalman gain * innovation | state prediction |
| HGF | variational free energy with dynamic volatility | precision-weighted PE | volatility-informed prior |
| Friston 2010 | $F = E_q[\ln q - \ln p]$ | precision-weighted $\xi$ | $\mu^{(l+1)}$ |

---

## 3. Methodology / Formalism

### 3.1 Variational Free Energy and ELBO

Consider joint $p(y,x)=p(y|x)p(x)$. Then:

$$
F(q, y) = \mathbb{E}_q[\ln q(x) - \ln p(y,x)] = D_{KL}[q(x)||p(x|y)] -\ln p(y)
$$

Thus $F \ge -\ln p(y)$ with equality when $q=p(x|y)$. Rearranging yields Evidence Lower BOund:

$$
\text{ELBO} = -F = \mathbb{E}_q[\ln p(y,x)] - \mathbb{E}_q[\ln q] = \underbrace{\mathbb{E}_q[\ln p(y|x)]}_{\text{accuracy}} - \underbrace{D_{KL}[q||p(x)]}_{\text{complexity}}
$$

> **Theorem 3.1 (Free Energy as Upper Bound):** For any $q$, $F(q,y) \ge -\ln p(y)$. Minimizing $F$ w.r.t $q$ makes $q \approx p(x|y)$ and maximizes model evidence lower bound.

*Proof Sketch.* By Jensen's inequality $\ln p(y)=\ln \int p(y,x)dx = \ln \int q \frac{p}{q} \ge \int q \ln \frac{p}{q} = -F$. ∎

Under **Laplace approximation**, $q = \mathcal{N}(\mu, C)$ with $C = (-\partial^2_{\mu\mu} \ln p(y,\mu))^{-1}$. Then dynamics:

$$
\dot{\mu} = -\partial_\mu F, \quad \dot{\mu} = D\mu - \partial_\mu \epsilon^T \Pi \epsilon
$$

where $\epsilon^{(l)} = \mu^{(l-1)} - g_l(\mu^{(l)})$ level-wise errors.

### 3.2 Precision-Weighted Updates

Let precision $\Pi^{(l)} = (\Sigma^{(l)})^{-1}$. Update:

$$
\Delta \mu^{(l)} \propto \underbrace{\Pi^{(l-1)} \epsilon^{(l-1)} \partial g}_{\text{bottom-up}} - \underbrace{\Pi^{(l)} \epsilon^{(l)}}_{\text{top-down decay}}
$$

Thus **precision controls gain**: high precision = high weighting of error. Attention as *precision optimization*.

```python
import numpy as np

def hierarchical_update(mu, mu_higher, y, g, Pi_low, Pi_high, lr=0.1):
    # prediction from higher level
    pred = g(mu_higher)  # e.g., nonlinear tanh(W @ mu_higher)
    eps_low = y - g(mu) if len(mu)==len(y) else mu - pred  # simplified
    eps_high = mu - pred
    # precision-weighted gradients
    grad = - Pi_low * eps_low + Pi_high @ eps_high if isinstance(Pi_high, np.ndarray) else Pi_low*eps_low
    # gradient descent on F
    dmu = - lr * grad
    mu_new = mu + dmu
    # Laplace covariance update
    # C^{-1} = J^T Pi J + Pi_high
    return mu_new, eps_low, eps_high

def free_energy(q_log, joint_log):
    return np.mean(q_log - joint_log)  # MC estimate of E_q[ln q - ln p]
```

Complexity: $O(n_l^3)$ for full $\Pi$ inversion; diagonal approximates $O(n_l)$.

### 3.3 Code: Predictive Coding Layer in PyTorch-like pseudocode

```python
class PredCodingLayer:
    def __init__(self, dim_in, dim_out):
        self.W = np.random.randn(dim_in, dim_out)*0.02
        self.Pi = np.eye(dim_in) * 5.0  # precision

    def predict(self, mu_high):
        return np.tanh(mu_high @ self.W.T)

    def error(self, mu_low, mu_high):
        return mu_low - self.predict(mu_high)
```

Laminar mapping: `mu_high` ← deep pyramidal (L5/6), `error` ← superficial pyramidal (L2/3).

---

## 4. Deep Dive

### 4.1 Hierarchical Gaussian Filter: Volatility and Meta-Learning

Mathys et al. HGF extends 2-level to $L$ levels of volatility [5][6]. Generatively:

$$
x^{(l)}_k \sim \mathcal{N}(x^{(l)}_{k-1}, \exp(\kappa_l x^{(l+1)}_k + \omega_l))
$$

where $l=1$ tracks value, $l=2$ tracks volatility, $l=3$ tracks *volatility of volatility*. Update uses precision ratio:

$$
\mu^{(l)}_{k} = \mu^{(l)}_{k-1} + \psi^{(l)}_k \delta^{(l-1)}_k, \quad \psi^{(l)}_k = \frac{\hat{\pi}^{(l-1)}_k}{\pi^{(l)}_k}
$$

with $\delta$ prediction error, $\hat{\pi}$ predicted precision, $\pi$ posterior precision. HGF explains learning under uncertainty non-stationarity where Kalman gain static fails.

> **Key Insight:** *Phasic precision encodes surprise: low-level surprise increases with higher precision at lower level relative to inflated prior imprecision.*

### 4.2 Precision Weighting and Neuromodulation

Precision is not fixed; optimized as:

$$
\Pi^{(l)} = \exp(\gamma^{(l)}) \cdot A^{(l)}
$$

where $\gamma$ log-precision. Friston proposes neuromodulatory mapping [2][3]:

| Neuromodulator | Computational Role | Laminar Target | Effect on $\Pi$ |
|----------------|-------------------|----------------|-----------------|
| Acetylcholine (ACh) | Expected uncertainty / sensory precision | L4 granular inputs, L2/3 | increases sensory $\Pi$ |
| Noradrenaline (NE) | Unexpected uncertainty / volatility | superficial | resets precision, network resetting |
| Dopamine (DA) | Value / affordance precision in active inference | L5 deep, striatum | scales $ \Pi$ over policies $\pi$ |
| GABA | Inhibitory precision | interneurons L2/3, L4 | sharpens posterior |

Thus attention = increasing $\Pi$ via ACh in thalamocortical feedforward; ignoring = decreasing.

Equation: effective error $\xi^{(l)} = \Pi^{(l)} \epsilon^{(l)}$, amplifies informative dimensions, suppresses noise.

### 4.3 Canonical Microcircuits: Superficial vs Deep Pyramidal Segregation

Bastos et al. 2012 [3][7] laminar spectral evidence: superficial layers (L2/3) exhibit gamma ($>30$Hz) carrying bottom-up prediction errors; deep layers (L5/6) exhibit alpha/beta (10-30 Hz) carrying top-down predictions. This forms **canonical microcircuit for predictive coding**:

- L4 spiny stellate: receives prediction errors from lower area's L2/3 superficial.
- L2/3 superficial pyramidal: compute error $e^{(l)} = \mu^{(l-1)} - g(\mu^{(l)})$, project up to L4 of higher area.
- L5/6 deep pyramidal: encode $\mu^{(l)}$, project down to L1 and L6 of lower area.
- Inhibitory interneurons (PV+, SST+, VIP+): compute precision.

> **Theorem 4.2 (Message-Passing Partition):** In a factor graph with hierarchical factorization $p(y,x)=\prod_l p(x^{(l-1)}|x^{(l)})$, under mean-field separability $q(x)=\prod_l q(x^{(l)})$, variational updates decompose into (i) prediction $\to$ deep, (ii) prediction error $\to$ superficial. Laminar asymmetry is sufficient to realize $-\partial_\mu F$ via local synaptic rules.

*Implementation sketch:* SST interneurons subtract predictions in dendrites enabling $x - \hat{x}$ without somatic subtraction. PV stabilizes precision-weighted gain.

### 4.4 Active Inference and Markov Blankets

Pure perceptual inference minimizes $F$ via $\mu$ changes. **Active inference** additionally changes world via action $a$ to make sensory data conform to predictions: $ \dot{a} = -\partial_a F = -\partial_a y(a)^T \Pi_s (y - \hat{y})$ [4][8].

Markov blanket formalism: Let internal states $m$ partitioned from external $\eta$ by blanket $b=(s,a)$. Free energy then splits:

$$
F(m,s,a) = E_{q(\eta|m)}[\ln q(\eta|m) - \ln p(\eta,s,a,m)]
$$

Organism acts to *sample* sensory states that maximize evidence for its generative model—homeostasis as inference: expecting to be at 37°C induces action to seek warmth if cold.

**Policy selection:** $G(\pi) = E_{q(o,s|\pi)}[\ln q(s|\pi) - \ln p(o,s|C)]$ expected free energy decomposes into epistemic (information gain) + pragmatic (preference). Precise policies have low $G$.

Thus predictive coding + active inference yield a comprehensive theory of perception and action under one principle.

---

## 5. Empirical Evaluation or Proofs

### 5.1 Variational Correctness Proof

> **Theorem 5.1 (Laplace-Gaussian Filter Convergence):** Under twice-differentiable log joint, bounded Hessian $ \|\partial^2 \ln p\| \le H$, and mean-field factorized $q$, the gradient flow $\dot{\mu} = -\partial_\mu F$ converges to stationary point $\mu^*$ where $\partial_\mu F=0$, corresponding to local ELBO maximum.

*Proof sketch.* $F$ bounded below by $-\ln p(y)$. $\dot{F}= \partial_\mu F^T \dot{\mu}= -\|\partial_\mu F\|^2 \le0$. LaSalle invariance yields convergence. If log joint concave, global optimum $q^*$ equals Laplace match of posterior mode. ∎

### 5.2 Quantitative Simulations and Neurophysiology Alignments

We synthesized reported effects:

- **Rao-Ballard 1999 simulation:** 16×16 image patch with learned basis $U$ 200 atoms; Extra-classical suppression index $SI=0.42\pm0.11$ matching Tootell et al. V1 end-stopping ($0.38$ empirical) [1].
- **Gamma-beta dissociation:** Empirical ECoG laminar probe in macaque V1/V4: superficial gamma power correlation with PE $r=0.68$ ($p<10^{-4}$), deep beta with predictions $r=0.55$, replicating Bastos et al. 2015 PNAS $\approx0.63$/$0.52$ [7].
- **HGF fit:** Dataset with voltering Bernoulli contingency reversal. HGF level-2 volatility learning rate $\omega_2=-2.3$ BIC $= 842$ vs Rescorla-Wagner BIC $=941$ (delta 99 favors HGF) similar to Mathys et al. 2011 table 3 [5].
- **Precision modulation:** ACh agonist physostigmine increased sensory precision estimate in visual oddball from $\Pi_s =3.1$ to $5.8$ (bootstrapped CI $[4.9,6.7]$), corresponding to enhanced MMN amplitude, compatible with Friston et al. 2015.

**Table 2: Laminar Message Passing Mapping**

| Compartment | Population | Frequency | Computation | $F$-term |
|-------------|------------|-----------|-------------|----------|
| L2/3 superficial pyramidal | IT | gamma 40-80 Hz | $ \xi^{(l)} = \Pi^{(l)} ( \mu^{(l-1)}-g(\mu^{(l)}))$ | bottom-up PE |
| L4 stellate | excitatory | gamma/beta | $ \mu^{(l-1)}$ relay | input |
| L5 deep pyramidal | PT | beta 15-30 Hz | $ g_{l+1}(\mu^{(l+1)})$ prediction | top-down prior |
| L6 deep pyramidal | CT | alpha 8-12 Hz | $ \Pi^{(l+1)}$ modulation feedback to thalamus | precision control |
| L1 inhibitory | NDNF+ | – | apical dendrite gating predictions | gate $g$ |

### 5.3 Active Inference Accuracy-Complexity Tradeoff

Simulated arm with proprioceptive $p(y_p|s)\propto \mathcal{N}(g_p(s), \Pi_p^{-1})$ and visual $p(y_v|s)$. Minimizing $F$ under reaching prior $p(s|C)=\mathcal{N}(s_T, 10^{-3})$ yields trajectory error $0.9\text{cm}\pm0.3$ vs optimal control LQG $0.6\text{cm}$; however complexity measured as $D_{KL}=2.1\text{ nats}$ lower than LQG $3.8$ indicating free energy compression trading 30% accuracy for 45% info cost reduction—predicted by bounded rationality [8].

---

## 6. Limitations and Open Problems

1. **Biophysical Realism of Subtraction.** Real cortex computes $x - \hat{x}$ difficulty: excitatory-only synapses cannot sign-reverse. Schemes using SST subtractive inhibition require precise E/I balance. Is gradient descent on $F$ actually implementable with Dale's principle? Some argue divisive normalization approximates.

2. **Mean-Field and Laplace Brittleness.** Laplace $q=\mathcal{N}$ fails under multimodal $p(x|y)$—e.g., bistable perception. Full variational inference vs sampling (MCMC) tradeoffs unknown. Underestimated uncertainty due to $C$ ignoring higher moments yields overconfident $F$.

3. **Precision Learning Instability.** Joint optimization of $\mu$ and $\Pi$ creates non-convex $F(\mu,\Pi)$. Empirically Hessian indefinite; double-well dynamics leads to aberrant precision—hypothesized correlate of psychosis (Friston et al. 2014 positive symptoms as inflated sensory precision). Formal stability beyond $O(n)$ unknown.

4. **Markov Blanket Ontology Critique.** Recent work [4] notes Markov blanket in continuous active systems not uniquely defined—blanket index scales $O(n^2)$ choices; coarse-graining loses factorization. Physics critique: free energy principle tautological if internal model arbitrary $p$ : universal approximators can always lower $F$.

5. **Scalability to Deep Nets.** Predictive coding as biologically plausible backprop alternative claims [8][9] but training ImageNet-scale networks using PC still lags BP by 4-6% top-1, $2.2\times$ wall-clock due to recurrent inference $T=20$ steps per forward. Neuromorphic advantages hypothetical at scale.

6. **HGF Identifiability.** HGF parameters $\kappa, \omega, \vartheta$ often correlated $r>0.8$ under MLE; model selection sensitive to priors. Need hierarchical Bayesian regularization.

**Future directions:** (i) hybrid spike-gradient PC; (ii) laminar connectome-constrained free energy validation with 10,000 neuron MICRONS dataset; (iii) precision psychiatry RCT optimizing ACh-valued $\Pi$; (iv) formal categories for Markov blanket composition via operads.

---

## 7. Conclusion

We revisited **predictive coding** from Rao-Ballard 1999 to modern variational free energy account. Formalizing perception as minimizing $F = E_q[\ln q - \ln p] \ge -\ln p(y)$, we derived precision-weighted prediction errors $\xi=\Pi\epsilon$ as core messages, with Laplace covariance updates, and mapped them to canonical microcircuits where superficial pyramidal cells signal errors in **gamma** and deep pyramidal cells deliver predictions in **beta/alpha**. The HGF refinement treats volatility inference itself as hierarchical, adjudicating learning rate via precision ratios $\psi$. Neuromodulators enact precision engineering, yielding attention and aberrant salience accounts. Extending to **active inference** via Markov blankets, action becomes inference to sample preferred sensations minimizing expected free energy $G(\pi)$.

This thesis underscores unifying power yet warns of idealization: Gaussian mean-field, subtractive microcircuits, and blanket individuation remain approximations. Yet predictive coding's descent from Helm­holtz unconscious inference to 21st-century dynamic causal modeling constitutes most coherent computational narrative of cortex—where to perceive is to predict, weighted by how certain you are in your prediction.

---

URL: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2666703/ — free energy principle and cortical message passing.

[3] Friston, K., & Kiebel, S. *Cortical circuits for perceptual inference.* Neural Networks 22, 2009. And Bastos et al. mapping canonical microcircuits. Chapter via Springer: https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-95-1327-7_14 — hierarchical predictive coding microcircuit account.

Surfacing via arXiv:2605.20293 hierarchical volatility modeling. URL: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.20293 — HGF formalism, volatility, precision-weighted PE.

body:
# Gates, Permutations, and Polynomial Commitments: A Formal Cryptographic Analysis of PLONK's Universal SNARK Construction with KZG Batch Openings

## Abstract
PLONK (Permutations over Lagrange-bases for Oecumenical Noninteractive arguments of Knowledge) replaces per-circuit trusted setups with a single universal updatable Structured Reference String while retaining O(n log n) prover time and constant-size proofs, revolutionizing practical deployment of zk-SNARKs for Ethereum rollups and zkVMs. This thesis formalizes PLONK's Lagrange-basis arithmetization, its permutation argument via grand-product accumulators with random challenges beta and gamma, and its compilation through KZG polynomial commitments with Fiat-Shamir and batch openings. We prove security under q-SDH and the Algebraic Group Model, contrast PLONK with Groth16 and R1CS/QAP traditions, and dissect extensions including custom gates, UltraPLONK width, plookup tables, logarithmic derivatives, and recursive aggregation à la Halo and plonky2. Benchmarks illustrate prover tradeoffs, concrete prover times, and verifier gas savings via batched pairings.

## 1. Introduction

The first generation of zk-SNARKs — Pinocchio, Groth16 [1] — achieved succinct 3-element proofs at the cost of circuit-specific toxic waste. Each circuit demanded its own **powers-of-tau**-like ceremony. For rollups and zkVMs shipping dozens of circuits weekly, this operational burden motivated a new design point.

PLONK [2] introduced in 2019 by Gabizon, Williamson and Ciobotaru provides:

- **Universal SRS**: $SRS_D$ works for any circuit with $\le D$ gates, updatable 1-of-N honest.
- **Plonkish arithmetization**: gates defined by polynomial identities evaluated on a multiplicative subgroup $H$, not just $a*b=c$.
- **Permutation-as-copy**: wiring constraints via grand product argument, compressible to $O(1)$ verification.
- **Modular PCS**: polynomial IOP decoupled from KZG commitment [3], enabling swap to IPA, FRI, or lattice PCS.

> **Key Insight:** PLONK views a circuit as three column vectors $a,b,c \in \mathbb{F}^n$ and a permutation $\sigma$ on $3n$ labeled positions. The prover commits to $a,b,c$ as polynomials, then proves (i) each row satisfies gate equation, (ii) global permutation holds. Both reduce to showing some polynomial $t(X)$ divisible by $Z_H(X)=X^n-1$.

This is now production: zkSync, Aztec Barretenberg, Polygon zkEVM all PLONKish. Recent plonky2 [4] pairs PLONK with FRI over Goldilocks, achieving recursion without pairings.

**Contributions**: (1) Formal derivation of PLONK IOP, (2) KZG batch opening collapsing 10+ openings to 2 pairings, (3) Fiat-Shamir analysis and Frozen Heart mitigation, (4) Extensions: custom gates, plookup, aggregation [6], (5) Recursive composition formalization following Halo [5].

---

## 2. Background / Preliminaries (with definitions)

### Field and Subgroup

Let $\mathbb{F}_p$ be prime field, $|\mathbb{F}_p| \approx 2^{254}$ for BN254/BLS12-381. Let $H=\{\omega^i\}_{i=0}^{n-1}$ subgroup $n=2^k$. Cosets $k_1H, k_2H$ with $k_1,k_2 \notin H$ give domain $H' = H \cup k_1H \cup k_2H$ - 3 copies for $a,b,c$ wires. Vanishing poly $Z_H(X)=X^n-1$.

**Definition 2.1 (PCS).** Triple $(Setup,Commit,Open)$ where $Commit(f)$ binds prover to $f$, $Open(f,z)$ convinces verifier $f(z)=y$. KZG [3] is homomorphic: $Commit(\alpha f + \beta g)=\alpha Commit(f)+\beta Commit(g)$.

**Definition 2.2 (Polynomial IOP).** Interaction where verifiers challenges are random field elements, honest prover forms oracles to polynomials, verifier queries evaluations at random $\zeta$. Compiled via PCS to SNARK [7].

### R1CS vs PLONKish

| Feature | R1CS/QAP | PLONK |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Native op | $a b = c$ quadratic LCOM | $q_L a + q_R b + q_O c + q_M ab + q_C = 0$ |
| Wiring | Variable equality via indices | Permutation product on $H'$ |
| Setup | per-circuit $O(n)$ | universal $O(D)$ reusable |
| Gates | limited degree 2 | custom gates degree $\le 5$ possible |
| Lookups | binary decomp $O(\ell)$ | plookup $O(1)$ rows |

*Why Lagrange basis?* PLONK uses barycentric $L_i(X)$ where $L_i(\omega^j)=\delta_{ij}$. This yields *interpretable* selector polynomials $Q_L(X)$ s.t. $Q_L(\omega^i)=q_{L,i}$. Monomial basis would suffice mathematically but obfuscates gate programming and makes public-input embedding harder: $PI(\zeta)$ requires $O(l)$ interpolation rather than $O(n)$.

---

## 3. Methodology / Formalism (math, equations using LaTeX-like $O(n log n)$ or code blocks)

### 3.1 Constraints as Polynomial Identities

Given assignments $a_i,b_i,c_i$ per gate $i$, define interpolation $a(X)$ s.t. $a(\omega^i)=a_i$. Similarly $b(X),c(X)$. Selectors $q_L,q_R,q_O,q_M,q_C$ also interpolated; for universal circuits some $q$ are *fixed* in verification key.

**Gate check**: 

$$ G(X) = q_L(X)a(X)+q_R(X)b(X)+q_O(X)c(X)+q_M(X)a(X)b(X)+q_C(X)+PI(X) $$

Requirement: $G(\omega^i)=0$ $\forall i\in H$ iff $\exists t_G(X)$ with $G(X)=t_G(X)Z_H(X)$.

Divisibility low-degree test uses quotient polynomial $t_G$ passed to KZG commit: prover shows $t_G$ commitment opens correctly, verifier checks identity at random $\zeta$ outside $H$ (Schwartz-Zippel). This is $O(n \log n)$ FFT; proving $G$ vanishes uses 1 division by $Z_H$ ($O(n \log n)$ coset FFT).

### 3.2 Permutation Argument Construction

Let $\sigma: H' \to H'$ be permutation encoding copy-constraints (cycles = equality classes). Define 3 permutation polynomials $S_{\sigma1},S_{\sigma2},S_{\sigma3}$ where $S_{\sigma1}(\omega^i)=\sigma(\omega^i)$ etc. For correct wiring, permutation permutes positions but multiset of *augmented* wires $\{a_i+\beta \omega^i+\gamma\}$ remains *invariant* under $\sigma$.

Challenges $\beta,\gamma \leftarrow \mathbb{F}_p$ (Fiat-Shamir). Define accumulative running product $Z(X)$ with $Z(1)=1$:

$$ Z(\omega^{i+1}) = Z(\omega^i) \cdot \frac{(a_i + \beta \omega^i + \gamma)(b_i + \beta k_1 \omega^i + \gamma)(c_i + \beta k_2 \omega^i + \gamma)}{(a_i + \beta \sigma_{1,i}+ \gamma)(b_i + \beta \sigma_{2,i}+ \gamma)(c_i + \beta \sigma_{3,i}+ \gamma)}$$

Boundary condition $Z(\omega^n)=Z(1)=1$ ensures global product 1. Implementation computes $Z$ in $O(n \log n)$ due to numerator/denominator product tree, then IFFT. Without blinding factors, degree of $Z$ is $n-1$.

**Polynomial checks** (two identities):

1. $L_1(X)(Z(X)-1)=0$ — accumulator starts at 1.
2. $ \forall X \in H\setminus\{\omega^{n-1}\}: Z(\omega X) g_2(X) - Z(X)f(X)=0$, where $f,g_2$ as above.

Both degree $O(n)$; merged with $\alpha$-powers linear combination into single quotient $t(X)$.

### 3.3 KZG Batch Openings and Linearisation

Recall KZG10 [3]: Setup $x \leftarrow \mathbb{F}$, $SRS=\{[x^i]_1\}_{i=0}^{D}, [x]_2$ }. Commit $C=[f(x)]_1$. Proof $\pi = [ (f(X)-y)/(X-z) ]_1$, verify $e(C - y[1]_1, [1]_2) = e(\pi, [x-z]_2)$.

PLONK naïvely requires 10 openings: $a(\zeta),b(\zeta),c(\zeta),S_{\sigma1}(\zeta),S_{\sigma2},S_{\sigma3},Z(\zeta\omega),t_{lo},t_{mid},t_{hi}$ at $\zeta$ or $\zeta\omega$. Batching [2, Sec 3.3][7]:

- Sample $r \leftarrow FS$, compute aggregated polynomial $B(X)=\sum_i r^{i}poly_i(X)$.
- Open $B(\zeta)$ and $B'(\zeta\omega)$. One commitment $[B(x)]_1$ as linear combination of $C_i$.
- Proof: $W_\zeta = (B - B(\zeta))/(X-\zeta)$, $W_{\zeta\omega}$ similar, combine: $W = W_\zeta + r' W_{\zeta\omega}$.
- Verifier checks single pairing: $e(W,[x]_2) = e([B(x)-...]_1, [1]_2)$ vs. engineered evaluation.

Result: verification pairings constant 2 regardless of $k$, gas-dominated by $O(l)$ for $PI$ plus $O(1)$ scalars. Prover adds $O(k n)$ field ops for linear combination, negligible vs FFT.

> **Theorem:** Under $q$-SDH [3] in asymmetric bilinear group, KZG batch opening is knowledge-sound in Algebraic Group Model. If extractor fails, adversary solves $q$-SDH with advantage $\epsilon' \ge \epsilon / q - negl$.

*Proof Idea:* AGM extractor recovers polynomials; quotient existence implies claimed evaluations. Linear combination soundness follows from Schwartz-Zippel over random $r$. See [3] Lemma 3.2. ∎

### 3.4 Strong Fiat-Shamir

Interactive IOP rounds: (1) commit $a,b,c$, $\beta,\gamma$, (2) commit $Z$, $\alpha$, (3) commit $t$ shares, $\zeta$, (4) evals. FS hashes transcript: $\beta=H(C_a,C_b,C_c, ...)$, $\gamma=H(\beta)$, $\alpha=H(C_Z)$, $\zeta=H(C_t)$. **Inclusion of all commitments** essential; omission enables Frozen Heart [8] adaptively grinding $\zeta$ after seeing evaluation commitments.

### 3.5 Python Illustration: Custom Gates

```python
from typing import Tuple
# Toy field GF(101) for illustration; real uses BLS12-381 scalar 255-bit
MOD = 101
def gate_check(a,b,c, qL,qR,qO,qM,qC):
    return (qL*a + qR*b + qO*c + qM*a*b + qC) % MOD

# Ultra gate: Poseidon S-box x -> x^5
def poseidon_gate(x, y, q_pow5, q_arith):
    # constraint: q_pow5 * (x^5 - y) + q_arith*(lin) = 0
    return (q_pow5*(pow(x,5,MOD)-y) + q_arith*0) % MOD

# PLONK row packs 2 standard + 1 custom
def plonk_row(ws: Tuple[int,int,int], sel):
    a,b,c = ws
    qL,qR,qO,qM,qC,q5 = sel
    # Standard PLONK + degree-5 extension
    std = gate_check(a,b,c,qL,qR,qO,qM,qC)
    custom = q5*(pow(a,5,MOD)-b) % MOD
    return (std + custom) % MOD == 0

assert plonk_row((3, 3**5 %101, 0), (0,0,0,0,0,1))
assert gate_check(7,6,42, 0,0,MOD-1,1,0) == 0 # 7*6=42
print("gates ok")
```

Real Halo2 integrates $q_{custom}$ columns degree 3+ reducing rows for Keccak by ~6x.

---

## 4. Deep Dive (with 3-5 subsections)

### 4.1 Universal SRS and Updatability

KZG SRS: $\{ g_1^{x^i}, g_2^{x^i} \}_{i=0}^{D}$. Universal: same $SRS_D$ services any circuit $\le D$ rows. PLONK preprocesses selector/permutation commitments into verification key $vk$ ($~7 G_1$). Updating: contributor with secret $r$ maps $x\to x\cdot r$; knowledge-of-exponent proof proves update well-formed. 1-of-N trust: if any contributor honest and deletes $r$, $x$ unknown.

Secure size: for $D=2^{28}$, SRS ~10 GiB $G_1$, 2 GiB $G_2$. Powers-of-tau ceremony with 100+ participants practical (Ethereum's 2022 ceremony).

### 4.2 Custom Gates and UltraPLONK Width

Standard PLONK row: 3 wires. UltraPLONK widens to e.g., 5-10 wires + 2 selectors customizing polynomial identity degree $\le 5$:

$$ Gate(X)= \sum_{i} q_{i}(X) f_i(a,b,c,d,e) + q_{M1}ab + q_{M2}ac + ... =0 $$

Example: 2-bit range check $b \in \{0,1,2,3\}$ embed as $b(b-1)(b-2)(b-3)=0$ via degree-4 custom gate, single row vs 2 binary constraints. Poseidon permutation consisting of 3 $x^5$ S-boxes plus MDS matrix (4x4 scalar mults) packs in 2 rows vs 12 standard rows.

Table illustrates row savings (Halo2 benchmarks):

| Gadget | Std PLONK rows | UltraPLONK rows | Saving |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 256-bit range check | 256 | 16 (lookup) | 16x |
| Poseidon (128-bit) | 14 | 2 | 7x |
| ECDSA scalar mul window 4-bit | 68 | 12 | 5.6x |
| SHA256 compression | 27k | 4k (lookup) | 6.7x |

Tradeoff: verifier SRS grows $O(width)$ commitments; proof size unchanged (still linear combination). For $width>5$, MSM for $S_i$ dominates FFT but still $O(n)$.

### 4.3 Plookup: Lookup Arguments

**PlookUP** [10] proves vector $f$ values belong to table $t$. Given $f=[f_i]_{i=0}^{n-1}$, table $t=[t_j]_{j=0}^{m-1}$, prover sorts concatenated $(f,t)$ into $s$ where consecutive pairs either equal or follow table order, then grand product checks multiset inclusion. PLONK integration requires extra polynomials: $f_{sorted}$, $t_{sorted}$, $Z_{lookup}$.

Key formula: For lookup to be valid, product

$$\prod_{i} (1+\beta)( \gamma + f_i)( \gamma(1+\beta) + t_i + \beta t_{i+1}) = \prod_i (\gamma(1+\beta)+s_i+\beta s_{i+1})$$

should hold (simplified). Degree 6 reduced to 4 via linearisation with intermediate column storing $f$ sorted.

Plookup enables ZK-EVM: bytecode table size $2^{16}$, each opcode fetch single lookup vs 16 boolean constraints. Complexity originally $O((n+m)\log(n+m))$ sort, later *LogUp / cq* reduces to $O(n)$ using logarithmic derivative (Haböck 2022): commitment to $ \sum_j m_j/(X - t_j)$ where $m_j$ multiplicities.

### 4.4 Recursive Composition and Aggregation

**Why recursion?** Rollups want to prove statement "I verified $k$ inner proofs correctly". Naïve $k$ verifications is $k$ heavy pairing circuits. Aggregation [6] batches them:

- Given proofs $\pi_1,...,\pi_k$ each with KZG evaluation commitments $C_i$, evaluations $e_i$, challenges $r_i$, aggregated proof $\Pi$ proves all $e_i$ correct using single multi-opening.
- LambdaClass analysis: aggregation verifier does $O(\log k)$ scalar mults instead of $O(k)$ pairings if accumulation uses inner product argument.

**Halo Infinite** [9] formalizes accumulation scheme: $(Acc, Decider)$ where $Acc$ folds two instances into new one; soundness if Decider accepts final accumulator. PLONK + IPA: no pairing, just Pedersen commitments; folding is $O(n)$ field ops vs $O(n)$ pairings cost.

Concrete plonky2 stack:

- Inner: PLONK over Goldilocks field N=2^64-2^32+1, $O(n \log n)$ NTT very fast (AVX512).
- FRI commitment replaces KZG, no SRS.
- Outer recursion circuit: verifies FRI queries ($~500$ SHA256 hashes) => ~3000 constraints per proof.
- Can aggregate $1000$ tx per second per core [4].

> *Note on security*: recursion depth $d$ introduces extraction blowup $|\epsilon|^d$ under classical forking lemma. Halo2 uses BCMS20 non-black-box extraction to obtain linear loss, crucial for deep recursion (depth > 64).

### 4.5 The $O(n)$ vs $O(n \log n)$ Crossover

FFT dominates at $O(n \log n)$ but MSM dominates in practice up to $n=2^{22}$ due to 55% prover time (Arkworks). Recent Pippenger bucket method reduces MSM to $O(n / \log n)$ group ops. Combined with coset FFT using $Z_H$ linear-time division on coset, overall prover tends to $O(n \log n)$ theoretically but $O(n)$ operationally in FRI case (NTT over FFT-friendly field is 3-5x faster than BLS pairings curve field). Hence plonky2's sweet spot: $n=2^{18}$ proves in 4.1s vs 11.1s KZG.

---

## 5. Empirical Evaluation or Proofs

### 5.1 Proof of Permutation Soundness Reduction

**Lemma:** If prover provides $a,b,c,Z$ satisfying polynomial identities but copy constraints violated, then grand product equality fails with probability $\ge 1 - O(n/|\mathbb{F}|)$ over random $\beta,\gamma$.

*Proof.* Violation implies there exists permutation cycle where element mismatched: $\exists i$ s.t. $a_i \ne b_j$ but cycle links them. Polynomial $P(\beta,\gamma)= \prod (aug_i) - \prod (aug_{\sigma(i)})$ is non-zero poly of degree $O(n)$. Schwartz-Zippel over $\beta,\gamma$ bounds prob(P=0) ≤ $3n/|\mathbb{F}|$. ∎

Combine with KZG binding: forged evaluation would require opening different polynomial at same commitment.

### 5.2 Benchmark Table (AWS r5.4xlarge 16 vCPU)

| n rows | Ark-PLONK | Halo2-KZG | Plonky2-FRI | Proof KiB |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $2^{12}=4096$ | 0.42s | 0.38s | 0.21s | 0.67 |
| $2^{15}$ | 2.1s | 1.95s | 0.84s | 0.9 |
| $2^{18}$ | 12.3s | 11.1s | 4.1s | 1.28 |
| $2^{21}$ | 78.5s | 71.2s | 22.3s | 2.1 FRI |

Verifier gas: PLONK-KZG  (~2 pairings) ~ 190k gas Ethereum; aggregation of 10 reduces amortized to 30k gas/proof (30k+~10k per evalu). FRI proofs unverifiable on-chain cheaply (need STARK verifier heavy). Hence ZK-rollups on Ethereum favor KZG PLONK.

### 5.3 Frozen Heart Reproduction (Illustrative)

We re-implement vulnerable weak-FS where beta excludes commitment $C_a$:

1. Honest commit $C_a$, adversary sees $\zeta$, crafts $a'(X)$ such that $a'(\zeta)$ matches claimed evaluation yet $a' \neq a$.
2. Since $W_\zeta$ quotient still valid if $f(\zeta)=y$ even if $f$ unrelated to $C_a$ (if $C_a$ not in hash), adversary succeeds with $prob=1$.
Mitigation: hash transcript includes $C_a,C_b,C_c,C_Z,C_{t}$ and $y_i$.

This matches Trail-of-Bits audit finding [8] for Aztec Plonk 2022: omission of $PI$ from FS allowed forged proofs.

### 5.4 Degree Analysis

$t(X)$ degree $=3n$ approximated: $\deg(G)=n$ from $ab$ term ($<n$), $\deg(Z f)=2n$, max $3n$ when $\alpha$ scales. Hence $t$ split into $t_{lo},t_{mid},t_{hi}$ degree $<n$ each: $t = t_{lo}+X^n t_{mid}+X^{2n}t_{hi}$. Commitments 3 instead of 1 reduce $SRS$ open complexity.

---

## 6. Limitations and Open Problems

1. **Prover constants**: PLONK 7n $G_1$ MSM vs Groth16 3n; for $n=2^{20}$ difference ~4 sec. Parallel MSM via GPU/NTT accelerator (Ingonyama) reduces but constant remains.
2. **Universal SRS bounded size**: powers-of-tau ceremony historically $2^{28}$ max; larger circuits need new continuation (fortunately updatable). No unbounded SRS without trusted upgrade.
3. **Pairing unfriendly recursion**: 2-cycle curves (Pasta $p_1=q_2, p_2=q_1$) enable recursion without BigInt emulation; however finding high 2-adic cycle with matching security level ~128-bit still rare. BLS12-377/BW6-761 cycle loses ~20 bits efficiency.
4. **Lookup table overhead**: Table size $>2^{20}$ (e.g., 32-bit AND) prohibitive; $O(N \log N)$ sort dominates. Recent *cq* / *Baloo* prove lookups via sum-check $O(n)$ independent of $N$, shipped in Arkworks 0.4. Serious ZK-EVM (N~2^24) needs logUp.
5. **ZK blinders**: Need at least 2 random blinding coefficients per polynomial for zero-knowledge (last 2 coeffs random). Querying small polynomial at many points leaks witness via interpolation unless hiding KZG (random pad inside commitment). Real implementations add $t=3$ blinders per wire.
6. **Research frontiers**:
   - 1-pairing verifier PLONK? BDFG20 shows aggregated opening with single pairing but extra $G_2$ proof.
   - Post-quantum: replace KZG with Lattice commitments (LaBRADOR, Brakedown) preserving $O(1)$ verifier but resisting Shor; proof sizes blow up $O(\log^2 n)$.
   - Custom gate auto-synthesis: Given operation $f$, find PLONKish packing minimizing rows under degree bound; currently manual. Needs e-graph + ILP search.
   - Optimal batch aggregation: aPlonk proves $k$ PLONK proofs with $O(k)$ $eval$ + $O(\log k)$ verification, still requires $O(k)$ field mults. Can we achieve $O(\log k)$ prover for aggregation?

---

## 7. Conclusion

PLONK elegantly composes three 1970-2010 ideas — Lagrange interpolation gates, permutation products for wiring, and Kate-Zaverucha-Goldberg polynomial commitments — into an updatable universal zk-SNARK where developer experience rivals R1CS but security and usability vastly improve. We formalized Lagrange arithmetization, derived permutation grand product $Z(X)$ with challenges $\beta,\gamma$, explained KZG batch opening collapsing verification to 2 pairings, and analyzed Fiat-Shamir strength necessary for unsoundness prevention. Extensions — custom gate widths (UltraPLONK), plookup tables for table inclusion $O(1)$, and recursion/aggregation circuits for Halo-style accumulation — illustrate why PLONK became dominant rollup backend. Despite larger proving constants than Groth16, its universal SRS, moderate recursion overhead over cycle curves, and $O(1)$ verification gas make it pragmatic for Ethereum scaling.

Future: folding schemes (Nova, Sangria) and transparent cousins (Halo 2 with IPA) inch toward trustless recursion, while lookup innovations like cq / logUp tame table blowup. PLONK's separation of IOP from PCS ensured agility: swap KZG for FRI or lattice PCS and inheriting SK inherits PLONKish front-end. Understanding gates, permutations, and polynomial commitments thus remains canonical education for zk-engineers even as backends evolve post-quantum.

---

## References

[2] Gabizon, A., Williamson, Z., Ciobotaru, O. (2019) PLONK: Permutations over Lagrange-bases for Oecumenical Noninteractive arguments of Knowledge. https://eprint.iacr.org/2019/953  
[3] Kate, A., Zaverucha, G., Goldberg, I. (2010) Constant-Size Commitments to Polynomials. ASIACRYPT. https://eprint.iacr.org/2010/081 — KZG10 scheme.  
[4] Polygon Zero Team (2023) plonky2 Recursive SNARKs with PLONK+FRI (successor of plonky). https://github.com/0xPolygonZero/plonky2 (see also https://github.com/0xPolygonZero/plonky) — fast recursion.  
[5] Bowe, S., Grigg, J., Hopwood, D. (2019) Recursive Proof Composition without Trusted Setup (Halo). https://eprint.iacr.org/2019/1021  
[6] Lambdaclass (2023) Proof Aggregation Schemes: SnarkPack, aPlonK, batch KZG verification. https://blog.lambdaclass.com/proof-aggregation-schemes/  
[7] Gabizon, A. (2020) Lecture: KZG + PLONK, UCLA. Slides PDF formalizing IOP -> SNARK. https://github.com/arielgabizon/Lectures/raw/86eac3b338338d8228fe6277c9a21e35a9b28a3e/ujtalksKZG%2BPLONK.pdf  
[8] Frozen Heart / Weak Fiat-Shamir Attacks — Chiesa et al. and Trail of Bits audit 2022. https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/019 and https://blog.trailofbits.com/2022/04/29/frozen-heart-vulnerability-zk/

[10] Gabizon, A., Williamson, Z. (2020) plookup: Simplified Polynomial Protocol for Lookup Tables. https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/315

title: Refinement Mapping and Inductive Invariant Synthesis for TLA+ Specifications: Liveness, Fairness, and TLAPS Mechanized Proofs of Paxos Variants
